members.title: US, China can help end Ukraine war, Trump tells Xi before trilateral with Putin
members.lead: Trump says US, China can help end war in Ukraine Trump calls Putin a “friend” Trump meets Xi, Putin separately before unprecedented trilateral Analysts say gathering is unlikely to produce major agreements . US President Donald Trump told his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping on Thursday that they should both help end the war in Ukraine ahead of their unprecedented three-way meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The diplomatic gathering of the leaders of the world’s largest nuclear powers is unlikely to produce major agreements, analysts say, given deep differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons and trade. But it has unnerved smaller countries that fear their interests might be disregarded. Trump met Putin and Xi separately ahead of the trilateral talks, calling the Russian leader a “friend”. The Kremlin said they discussed Ukraine and that Putin left the meeting in an “excellent” mood. When meeting Xi right after, Trump thanked him for a lavish welcome and expressed hope that their trilateral with Putin would be successful. . “We’re looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine,” Trump said. “I’d like to see it ended.” Trump said both presidents felt strongly about oil having to flow through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been disrupted by the Iran war. Xi did not mention Ukraine or Iran in his remarks. Patricia Kim, foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution, said China would not want to be seen as brokering a deal over Ukraine, given the “problematic optics” of Kyiv and European leaders not taking part. . “Xi has characterized the Russia-Ukraine war as fundamentally a European problem, making Beijing even less inclined to assume responsibility for resolving it,” Kim said. . members.title: Badenoch says using amputee athletes to justify cutting disability benefits was ‘message of hope’ – UK politics live
members.lead: PM has asked Badenoch to withdraw her suggestion that benefits should be cut because ‘double amputees run marathons’ These are from my colleague Peter Walker, who was at the Tory event where James Cleverly was named as the party’s candidate for London mayor. Peter posted this before the result was announced. Khan (who may or may not stand a 4th time) has thus far faced a dilettante who decided to campaign on a racist platform (Zack Goldsmith) and two oddballs in Shaun Bailey and then Susan Hall. Not even he can be lucky yet again Interesting that [the Conservatives] did not say how many votes were cast, just the percentage - which perhaps indicates it was not a huge number Cleverly’s speech is mainly an attack on Labour and Khan, which is likely to be a theme for his campaign: “Burnham can’t stand London and Khan stand up to Burnham.” Also a pitch about building houses and cutting crime, and boosting transport. Cleverly says he would “end Khan’s war on motorists”, which is a sign he might lean into the anti-cycling and walking rhetoric which the London Tories have a habit of espousing. Expect talk about LTNs and 20mph zones. In the media Q&A Cleverly is pinned down on whether he backs the Tory party line on wanting to leave the ECHR and opposes net zero. He confirms he does (as he has to). Such things will be ready ammunition for Labour. Cleverly says of Andy Burnham, “His residual behaviour is to be anti-London”. This will very much be a theme of his campaign, it seems. Not sure how resonant a “poor London!” message will be even in London People are leaving London, or not choosing to come here in the first place, businesses, job creators, families leaving London, and by the time of the election in 2028, Khan will have been mayor for 12 years, and those two things are related. The problems London faces are the symptoms. Khan is the cause. Continue reading...
